notes.text: That they should gather a double portion on the sixth day, ver. 22-26.
That they should expect none on the seventh day, ver. 27-31,

That they should preserve a pot of it for a memorial, ver 32.

1. A month's provision, it seems, the host of Israel took with them out of Egypt, when they came thence on the 15th day of the first month, which, by the 15th day of the second month, was all spent.

2. Then the whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron - God's viceregents among them.

3. They so undervalue their deliverance, that they wish, they had died in Egypt, nay, and died by the hand of the Lord too. That is, by some of the plagues which cut off the Egyptians; as if it were not the hand of the Lord, but of Moses only, that brought them into this wilderness. 'Tis common for people to say of that pain, or sickness, which they see not second causes of, It is what pleaseth God, as if that were not so likewise which comes by the hand of man, or some visible accident. We cannot suppose they had any great plenty in Egypt, how largely soever they now talk of the flesh-pots, nor could they fear dying for want in the wilderness while they had their flocks and herds with them; but discontent magnifies what is past, and vilifies what is present, without regard to truth or reason. None talk more absurdly than murmurers.

4. Man being made out of the earth, his Maker has wisely ordered him food out of the earth, Psalm civ, 14. But the people of Israel typifying the church of the first-born that are written in heaven, receiving their charters, laws and commissions from heaven, from heaven also they received their food. See what God designed in making this provision for them, that I may prove them whether they will walk in my law or no - Whether they will trust me, and whether they would serve him, and be ever faithful to so good a master.
They shall prepare — Lay up, grind, bake or boil.
The Lord — And not we, (as you suggest) by our own counsel.
The glory of the Lord — An extra-ordinary and sudden brightness.

And ye shall know that I am the Lord your God — This gave proof of his power as the Lord, and his particular favour to them as their God; when God plagued the Egyptians, it was to make them know that he is the Lord; when he provided for the Israelites, it was to make them know that he was their God.

The quails came up, and covered the camp — So tame that they might take up as many of them as they pleased. Next morning he rained manna upon them, which was to be continued to them for their daily bread.

What is this? Manna descended from the clouds. It came down in dew melted, and yet was itself of such a consistency as to serve for nourishing strengthening food, without any thing else: It was pleasant food; the Jews say it was palatable to all, according as their tastes were. It was wholesome food, light of digestion. By this spare and plain diet we are all taught a lesson of temperance, and forbidden to desire dainties and varieties.
Glory — Glory in the God whom you serve, as the only true God.
Seek — The Lord in his strength, in his sanctuary, or before the ark, which is called God's strength. Face - His gracious presence.
Judgments — The punishments which he brought upon Egypt by his mere word.
Of Jacob — The only branch of Abraham's seed to whom the following blessings belong.
To me to live is Christ — To know, to love, to follow Christ, is my life, my glory, my joy.

Here he begins to treat of the former clause of the preceding verse. Of the latter he treats, chap. ii, 17. But if I am to live is the flesh, this is the fruit of my labour — This is the fruit of my living longer, that I can labour more. Glorious labour! desirable fruit! in this view, long life is indeed a blessing. And what I should choose I know not - That is, if it were left to my choice.
To depart — Out of bonds, flesh, the world. And to be with Christ - In a nearer and fuller union. It is better to depart; it is far better to be with Christ.
I know — By a prophetic notice given him while he was writing this. That I shall continue some time longer with you - And doubtless he did see them after this confinement.

Only — Be careful for this, and nothing else. Stand fast in one spirit - With the most perfect unanimity. Striving together - With united strength and endeavours. For the faith of the gospel - For all the blessings revealed and promised therein.
Which — Namely, their being adversaries to the word of God, and to you the messengers of God. Is an evident token - That they are in the high road to perdition; and you, in the way of salvation.
For to you it is given — As a special token of God's love, and of your being in the way of salvation.
Having the same kind of conflict with your adversaries, which ye saw in me — When I was with you, Acts xvi, 12, 19, &c.

That some of those who were first called may yet be last, our Lord confirms by the following parable: of which the primary scope is, to show, That many of the Jews would be rejected, and many of the Gentiles accepted; the secondary, That of the Gentiles, many who were first converted would be last and lowest in the kingdom of glory; and many of those who were last converted would be first, and highest therein. The kingdom of heaven is like — That is, the manner of God's proceeding in his kingdom resembles that of a householder. In the morning - At six, called by the Roman and Jews, the first hour. From thence reckoning on to the evening, they called nine, the third hour; twelve, the sixth; three in the afternoon, the ninth; and five, the eleventh. To hire labourers into his vineyard - All who profess to be Christians are in this sense labourers, and are supposed during their life to be working in God's vineyard.
The Roman penny was about seven pence halfpenny. [About thirteen and three quarter cents, American.] This was then the usual price of a day's labour.
About the eleventh hour — That is, very late; long after the rest were called.
In the evening — Of life; or of the world.

Who were hired about the eleventh hour — Either the Gentiles, who were called long after the Jews into the vineyard of the Church of Christ; or those in every age who did not hear, or at least understand the Gospel call, till their day of life was drawing to a period. Some circumstances of the parable seem best to suit the former, some the latter of these senses.
The first supposed they should have received more — Probably the first here may mean the Jews, who supposed they should always be preferred before the Gentiles.

Thou hast made them equal to us — So St. Peter expressly, Acts xv, 9. God-hath put no difference between us (Jews) and them, (Gentiles, ) purifying their hearts by faith. And those who were equally holy here, whenever they were called, will be equally happy hereafter.

It is my will to give to this last called among the heathens even as to the first called among the Jews: yea, and to the late converted publicans and sinners, even as to those who, were called long before.

Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own? — Yea, doubtless, to give either to Jew or Gentile a reward infinitely greater than he deserves. But can it be inferred from hence, that it is lawful, or possible, for the merciful Father of spirits to "Consign an unborn soul to hell? Or damn him from his mother's womb?" Is thine eye evil because I am good - Art thou envious, because I am gracious? Here is an evident reference to that malignant aspect, which is generally the attendant of a selfish and envious temper.

So the last shall be first, and the first last — Not only with regard to the Jews and Gentiles, but in a thousand other instances. For many are called - All who hear the Gospel; but few chosen - Only those who obey it. Matt. xix, 30; xxii, 14.

notes.text: It — The divine forbearance sparing Nineveh.
Was not this — Did I not think of this? That thy pardon would contradict my preaching.
Than to live — Disgraced and upbraided by hardened sinners, who will brand me for a liar.
A booth — Some small and mean shed, probably of green boughs. 'Till he might see - It seems the forty days were not fully expired.

Prepared — Commanded that in the place where Jonah's booth stood, this spreading plant should spring up to be a shade when the gathered boughs were withered. To deliver - To give some ease to his mind.
Prepared — By the same power which caused the gourd suddenly to spring, and spread itself. It smote - Which early next morning, bit the root, so that the whole gourd withered.

A east wind — A dry, scorching, blasting wind. Fainted - Overcome by the heat. Better to die - But Jonah must be wiser, and humbler, and more merciful too, e'er he die. Before God hath done with him, he will teach him to value his own life more, and to be more tender of the life of others.
I do well to be angry — If in the violence of this passion I should die (as some have) yet were I not to blame. What a speech! Verily the law made nothing perfect!
laboured — Thou didst not set it. Grow - Nor didst thou water or give growth to it.

I — The God of infinite compassions and goodness. That great city - Wouldest thou have me less merciful to such a goodly city, than thou art to a weed? Who cannot discern - Here are more than six-score innocents who are infants. Much cattle - Beside men, women and children who are in Nineveh, there are many other of my creatures that are not sinful, and my tender mercies are and shall be over all my works. If thou wouldest be their butcher, yet I will be their God. Go Jonah, rest thyself content and be thankful: that goodness, which spared Nineveh, hath spared thee in this thy inexcusable frowardness. I will be to repenting Nineveh what I am to thee, a God gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and I will turn from the evil which thou and they deserve.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The landowner went out at dawn, and at noon, and at the eleventh hour.
The Lord is good to all, and his mercy is over all.
Are you envious because I am generous?
The Lord is gracious and slow to anger.
We who came late are paid in full.
Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised.
Come, let us worship the God whose grace offends our arithmetic.
We come to the generous God. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Stand in the marketplace as the long day ends, the light going gold, certain you have been passed over — and hear the voice that says, you also, come.
The Lord is gracious and good to all.
We keep our ledgers of who worked longest and who deserves the most.
The Lord is gracious and good to all.
But God opens his hand to the latecomer, the outsider, even to Nineveh, even to us.
The Lord is gracious and good to all.
The first will be last and the last first, and the wage is the same: grace.
The Lord is gracious and good to all.
So come, whatever the hour, and receive what you could not earn.
The Lord is gracious and good to all. Thanks be to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: At the eleventh hour the call still comes: you also, come.
God is good to all.
We count who deserves the most.
God is good to all.
But grace is not a wage; it is a gift.
God is good to all.
Come, whatever the hour, and worship.
We come to the generous God. Amen.

turn.gravity: The day pairs Jonah — furious on his hill that God spared Nineveh — with the Psalm's slow-to-anger mercy and the vineyard's equal denarius. One nerve runs through all three: God's generosity offends the deserving. Grace is not fair, and the longest-serving resent it most.
turn.trap: It becomes a lesson about fairness (and how the workers should have read the fine print), or a warm word that "God rewards everyone" — either way the scandal is explained off. The parable's offense is precisely the equal wage; defuse it and there is no sermon left.
turn.hinge: The householder does no one wrong — every promise is kept — and the first are still furious. Grace that is genuinely unfair to our accounting. The only question the text leaves open is whether you can rejoice in that or only resent it.

doors.claim: The wage is eternal life itself, and it is given whole to everyone — heaven is not a pay scale, and the latecomer is not shortchanged.

witnesses.author: Origen
witnesses.reading: The denarius here I take to mean salvation itself.

witnesses.author: Augustine
witnesses.reading: Because life eternal shall be equal to all the saints, one denarius is given to all — though in that life the light of merits will still shine diversely.

witnesses.author: Jerome
witnesses.reading: The denarius bears the figure of the King: you have received my image and likeness. What more do you desire?

doors.say: What you are paid is God's own life, given to you entire — there is no larger wage to envy.
doors.do: Lead them to receive the denarius as gift, not earnings — to name where they have been counting their hours instead of marvelling at the coin.

doors.claim: The hours are the ages of the world; the last hired are the latecomers — the Gentiles, the deathbed convert, anyone called after us — and they are seated as our equals.

witnesses.author: Gregory the Great
witnesses.reading: The morning is the age from Adam to Noah, the third hour Noah to Abraham, the sixth and ninth to Moses and to the Lord, and the eleventh hour from the Lord's coming to the end of the world.

witnesses.author: John Wesley
witnesses.reading: The eleventh hour: the Gentiles, called long after the Jews into the vineyard of the Church — or those in any age who were called late.

doors.say: You may have worked since morning, but the kingdom is not seniority — the one called at the eleventh hour sits beside you, equal.
doors.do: Turn long-time members from a claim of priority to gladness at the latecomer — one person they would secretly rank below themselves.

doors.claim: The laborers were not cheated of anything; their grievance is simply that others got more than they deserved — and that envy of grace is the sin the parable exposes in us.

witnesses.author: Remigius of Auxerre
witnesses.reading: By the eye is meant the purpose: they had an evil eye, an evil purpose, because they were grieved at the salvation of the others.

witnesses.author: Pseudo-Chrysostom
witnesses.reading: Their complaint was not that they were defrauded of their wage, but that the others received more than they deserved — for the envious have as much pain at another's good as at their own ill.

doors.say: Search the resentment in your own chest when grace runs to someone who didn't earn it — that evil eye, not the wage, is the danger here.
doors.do: Send them, like Jonah left outside the city, to one place they are angry that God has been merciful, and to repent of the grudge.

synthesis.convergence: Jonah sulks that grace reached his enemies; the Psalm praises a God who is good to all and slow to anger; Paul counts his own advantage as nothing next to Christ and others; and the laborers seethe at an equal wage. Together they press one nerve: God's generosity offends the deserving.
synthesis.claim: Grace is not fair — and that is the best news in the world, unless you have been keeping count of your hours.
synthesis.here: For long-faithful church people — the first-hired, the elder brothers, the Jonahs — the move is to catch the resentment in their own chest when grace runs to the latecomer, and to let God's gentle 'are you angry?' turn them from the gate back to the feast.

turn.subtract: Three doors, three landings — wonder at the equal coin, humility before the latecomer, repentance of the evil eye. They cannot all be preached at once; pick the one your people most need and let the other two go.
turn.source: Catena Aurea (Aquinas; J.H. Newman tr., public domain) + Wesley's Explanatory Notes, retrieved from ~/reception-corpus — attested, not authored.
